State divergence between the recovery path and the ordinary insert path\n\n**Ordinary insert** (`src/db/index/segment/segment.cc:903-918`): `Insert()` calls `append_wal(doc)` first. `append_wal()` lazily calls `open_wal_file()` (`segment.cc:4324-4340`), which assigns the member `wal_file_` (`segment.cc:4303-4322`), then appends the record. `internal_insert()` then populates the memory components (`segment.cc:837-881`). No forward (SCALAR) block for the recovered docs is ever written or recorded.\n6. **Reopen in a third process**: `CollectionImpl::recovery()` opens the old segment from `v.persisted_segment_metas()` read-only (`collection.cc:1861-1874`); `SegmentImpl::Open` finds no `writing_forward_block`, so `recover()` is **skipped** (`segment.cc:484-510`). The WAL file — still on disk, since the no-op flush never reached `wal_file_->remove()` (2305-2315) — is orphaned: nothing derives its path anymore. The persisted blocks don't cover the docs.
